overview.title: Tall cedars and opportunistic monkeys
overview.p1: The cedar forests around Ifrane and Azrou are home to Barbary macaques and some of Morocco’s finest Atlas cedar stands. Trails and roadside stops make the forest accessible without serious mountaineering.
overview.p2: The monkeys are used to visitors. Keep food sealed, do not feed them, and step back if they approach. The forest is the point — not a photo chase.
overview.p3: Morning light under the canopy is beautiful. Pair with Dayet Aoua or continue to Azrou’s cedar market the same day.

q1.question: Is entry free?
q1.answer: Forest access is generally open; some organised stops may charge parking or guiding.

q2.question: Are monkeys dangerous?
q2.answer: They can snatch bags and food. Do not feed or corner them.

q3.question: Best time?
q3.answer: Morning for cooler air and better light under the canopy.

q4.question: Need a guide?
q4.answer: Not required for a short stop; useful for longer trails.

q5.question: Combine with?
q5.answer: Dayet Aoua, Azrou or return to Ifrane.

food.title: Eat around the forest
food.p1: Do not eat near monkeys with open bags. Snack in the car or back in town.
food.p2: Azrou has more lunch options if you continue that way.

tips.title: Practical Tips for the Cedar Forest

1.title: Secure your bags
1.desc: Zip everything. Macaques open loose pockets fast.

2.title: Stay on paths
2.desc: Protect roots and undergrowth; the forest is a living resource.

3.title: Weather shifts
3.desc: Altitude means sudden cool cloud — keep a layer in the car.
